senses.gloss: m. (<cite ref="C01320"><he>גרי</he></cite>, <cite ref="C01392"><he>גרר</he></cite>; cmp. b. h. <cite ref="U01268"><he>שֶׁלַח</he></cite>)

units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 37:33">Targ. Is. XXXVII, 33</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 41:20">Targ. Job XLI, 20</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Gittin 56a:6">Gitt. 56ᵃ</cite> <he>שדא ג׳ וכ׳</he> he shot an arrow eastward.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 26b:10">B. Kam. 26ᵇ</cite> <he>בעידנא דשדייה פסוקי מפסקי גִירֵיה</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) at the time he let his arrow off, its force was broken, i.e. when he threw the vessel down, polsters were there to prevent its breaking.
<cite ref="Sukkah 38a:1">Succ. 38ᵃ</cite> <he>דין ג׳ בעיניה וכ׳</he> this is an arrow in the tempter’s eyes, i.e. this enables us to defy him.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 30a:1">Kidd. 30ᵃ I</cite> should say to Satan <he>ג׳ בעיניך</he> I defy thee; <cite ref="Kiddushin 81a:15">ib. 81ᵃ</cite>.—
<cite ref="Taanit 25a:14">Taan. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>אגרי בך גִירַי</he> I shall let my arrow loose against thee (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note; oth. vers. v. <cite ref="C00474"><he>גּוּר</he></cite> I ch.).

<cite ref="Pesachim 28a:5">Pes. 28ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="C00810"><he>גִּירָאָה</he></cite>; a. fr.—<he>ג׳ דלילתא</he> (Ar. <he>דלוליתא</he>) the arrow of Lilith, supposed to be a wedge-shaped meteoric stone.
Gitt. 69ᵇ לגירא ליתי ג׳ דל׳ as a remedy for gira (v. preced.) let one get a gira of &c.—Pl. גִּירִין, גִּירֵי, גִּירַיָּא; גִּירְרִין, גִּירְרַיָּא.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 1:22">Targ. II Sam. I, 22</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 49:23">Targ. Y. I Gen. XLIX, 23</cite>, <cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 49:23">Targ. Y. II, Gen. XLIX, 23</cite> (not <he>גיד׳</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 120:4">Targ. Ps. CXX, 4</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 108b:21">Snh. 108ᵇ</cite> <he>גילי והוו ג׳</he> he threw chaff and it turned into arrows.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 73a">B. Bath. 73ᵃ</cite>; v. <he>בְּזַק</he>. Y. ib. II, 13ᵇ bot. <he>מן קל גורי וכ׳</he> (corr. acc.) from the hissing sound of the arrows; a. fr.
Sabb. 109ᵇ ג׳ דרוביא shoots of fenugreek; (oth. opin. in Ar. flax-seeds, Ms. O. גידא, v. גִּידָּא I).
